LESSON: WRITING 8.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: • NARRATIVE COMPOSITION (120 -160 WORDS) • SIMILES AND PROVERBS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing: • Narrative Composition (120 -160 words) • Similes and Proverbs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing: • Narrative Composition (120 -160 words) • Similes and Proverbs, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do we make our compositions interesting? 2. Which similes and proverbs do you know?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify similes and proverbs in a variety of texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing: • Narrative Composition (120 -160 words) • Similes and Proverbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use similes and proverbs correctly in oral and written texts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing: • Narrative Composition (120 -160 words) • Similes and Proverbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a narrative composition featuring similes and proverbs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 8.4.1 Creative Writing: • Narrative Composition (120 -160 words) • Similes and Proverbs in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. advocate the use of similes and proverbs to enhance creativity in writing. Learner is guided to: • Read narratives with formulaic expressions in print and digital format. • List similes and proverbs in texts collaboratively. • Create a clear and coherent storyline using proverbs and similes. • Engage in a dialogue to advance plot and storyline, • Compose a story featuring similes and proverbs with peers, • Write creative compositions featuring similes and proverbs, individually, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or be supported by peers, learner support assistants or scribe to write. 1. How do we make our compositions interesting? 2. Which similes and proverbs do you know? 72 ● Create and display charts with proverbs and similes, in pairs or small groups. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted by learner support assistant to create and display the charts.
